reasons: Claimed status is compliant for a direction-type rule that only bites when an MFN burdens our party; no redline or comment was proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited paragraph (Section 9.3 Expenses) and the surrounding Article IX context contain no most-favoured-nation, best-pricing, or third-party-offer-matching construct, and the rationale documents targeted searches ('most favored', 'no less favorable', 'pricing') that returned nothing — consistent with the preferred position of no MFN obligation on Customer.
Redline text is byte-identical to the original and no deterministic checks failed, so there is no risk of an unintended substantive change or over-flagging.

Minor: the anchor paragraph is only loosely related to the rule (an expenses clause used as a proxy for absence), but that is acceptable for an absence-based compliant finding retained as internal evidence.
